title: Rosa Weber and Other Retired Justices Call for Investigation into STF Crisis
seoTitle: Retired Justices, incl. Rosa Weber, Seek STF Crisis Probe
subtitle: Letter Signed by Rosa Weber, Joaquim Barbosa, and Other Former Justices Demands Public Session to Investigate Facts Affecting the Court
excerpt: Thirteen former STF justices, including Rosa Weber, sent a request to the Court's president for an urgent public session to investigate facts that.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
A letter signed by thirteen former justices of the Supreme Federal Court, including Rosa Weber, was released this Monday (7) and generated intense media interest. The document requests that the Court's president, Edson Fachin, immediately convene a public session for the plenary to determine a rigorous investigation of the facts that, according to the signatories, threaten public trust and the stability of democratic institutions.

The Call for Immediate Investigation

In the statement addressed to Fachin, the retired justices classify the moment as the “most acute crisis” in the Supreme Court's history. They request that the plenary, under due process of law, investigate the “extremely serious facts” whose disclosure has been compromising the Tribunal's prestige and authority.

Confidence in Fachin's Leadership

The text highlights “full confidence in Edson Fachin's seriousness, discernment, and firmness” in leading the Court. The signatories believe that the president will urgently schedule the requested session, ensuring respect for the rules and guarantees provided for the investigation.

Who Signed the Letter

In addition to Rosa Weber, the list includes Joaquim Barbosa, Ayres Britto, Celso de Mello, Nelson Jobim, Ellen Gracie, among others. The statement does not mention the names of currently serving justices nor does it specify the episodes that should be investigated.

Celso de Mello's Reaction

Following the motion's release, former justice Celso de Mello stated that the document does not refer to specific cases but maintains equidistance regarding the events that have caused a loss of social trust in the integrity, impartiality, and independence of the STF judges. He emphasized that “no authority is above the law” and advocated for public trials and examination of the facts by the plenary.

Objective of the Request

The retired justices emphasize that justice exercised in the name of the people must occur under society's observation, avoiding the “corrosive shadow of suspicion” and “unjustified secrecy.” The request aims to prevent illicit conduct or ethically reprehensible behaviors from casting doubt on the Court.

Expected Next Steps

If Fachin grants the request, the plenary should open a public session to deliberate on the investigation, observing due process. The decision will be closely watched, given the impact highlighted by the former justices on the Judiciary's credibility.

With information from G1, Gazeta do Povo.
